title: Game writing
author: BugaiGames
selftext:
Anyone get good writing from Claude for choices/events etc? So far most I get quite sloppy, missing logic and gives boring gameplay, so I'm rewriting everything manually, using AI only for high level ideas brainstorm.

So far it has become the biggest bottle neck outpacing image generation and UI that got pretty well with workflows and some tools to manage  assets.

comments.author: KnownPride
comments.body:
oh i'm thinking on making this, but i know ai model today both codex and clause sck at writing and creating plot. Well it's not like they're good at making fun gameplay loop at all.

So what kind of challenge you met? and what kind of game you make?

replies.author: BugaiGames
replies.body:
It is very niche node traversal time loop game. Eg you have map of connected nodes with "actions"/choices (gather fruits/ talk with guard/ investigate pattern). So basically gameplay+story merged together. But actions are simple, not VN level as Im bad in writing that format suits me.

There is some potion brewing, effects and stats mechanics ao it is not just reading fest and require branching and balancing.

Main problem that text hard to read due sloppinest and choices uninteresting, no connection between different branches and often illogical

comments.author: allangod
comments.body: As in story writing? No, i get passable story writing that will need actual thought to be any better than generic which is what i'd expect from AI.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
No, 

A fundamental problem with writing is that the LLMs have digested so much data... and a lot of that data is going to be mediocre writing. It's the same with things like golden hour lighting - it's in so many images that the LLM applies it where it doesn't belong.

To get good writing, someone will have to set-up a dedicated LLM for that and literally only feed it good literature. And, so far, there's no incentive to do that because such a machine would be hyper-specialized to a domain that doesn't make a lot of money.

comments.author: Dramatic_Leopard679
comments.body: I tried, and it's impossible to make it really natural and have ideal prose. I am not a good writer, but writing again and again improved me a lot. so drop the claude and grab the pen. it will be shorter and more original. and I personally wouldn't care much about AI written dialogue too even if I am not strict about art or code.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
AI story writing will be generic, stereotypical, bland, and predictable. It uses the same names, concepts, and shit all the time. If I'm making a fantasy setting and let Claude name people, I'm guaranteed to have a Kael. And it's probably the first name chosen. If I'm making a space themed game, that shit will absolutely have Starfall in the name somewhere.

Don't use AI for story or choices or dialogue.

replies.author: BugaiGames
replies.body:
I had better experience with dedicated story writing models, they gave me some surprises and interesting turns in small stories.
Problem that you get or prose or at least some reasoning. And game writing needs both
